project: Iron and Blood, a deterministic socioeconomic simulation in Rust with a Godot client

docs.homes: docs/README.md's table: rules in DECISIONS.md; mechanism in the system documents (ECONOMY_SYSTEM, POP_SYSTEM, POLITICS_SYSTEM, MACROECONOMICS, MAP_AND_LOGISTICS); Rust structure in BACKEND_SCHEMA.md; file formats in DATA_FORMAT.md; the wire protocol in NETWORK_PROTOCOL.md; measurements in PERFORMANCE.md; users in ONBOARDING.md and HOSTING.md
docs.milestoneRow: tick the task's row in the milestone document with a sentence or two on what was done (docs/README.md, "Milestone lifecycle")

env: export CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$ROOT/target/sdlc"   # one build cache for every agent of the run
full: for s in scenarios/mini_valley scenarios/two_states; do for t in 1 4; do cargo run --release -p pax_cli -- verify "$s" --threads "$t" || exit 1; done; done
cargo build --release -p pax_cli && PAX_CLI="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release/pax_cli" PAX_CLI_REQUIRED=1 cargo test --release -p pax_server --test session_replay
docs: scripts/render-mermaid.sh <each changed Markdown file with a mermaid block> (needs Docker; without it the step is skipped, not passed)
conditional: If schemas/ changed since origin/main: scripts/gen-protocol.sh && git diff --exit-code crates/pax_protocol/src/generated (then restore that directory).
If crates/pax_godot or client/ changed: cargo build -p pax_godot -p pax_server && PAX_SERVER="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug/pax_server" cargo test -p pax_godot
Mermaid: scripts/render-mermaid.sh on every Markdown file changed since origin/main that contains a mermaid block (needs Docker; without it the step is skipped, not passed).

engineering: Fixed only in simulation state and anything that feeds it; no floats (D3).
No std HashMap or HashSet where iteration order matters; randomness only through pax_engine::rng (D3).
Every split of a total uses alloc::allocate; every new money flow gets a case in crates/pax_engine/tests/conservation.rs, extending tests/common/mod.rs (D5).
No IO, rendering or networking in pax_engine; crate boundaries as AGENTS.md §2 sets them.
Every new column is pushed in its table's push_* method and added to World::state_hash; derived data is never stored (D7, D8).
Rustdoc explains the why and the mathematics and cites its D#.
A change to a hot loop is benchmarked against the D13 budget (pax_cli bench --scale 170000 --threads 8).

design.analysis: Arithmetic is in Fixed terms, with the rounding direction of each operation (mul/div round down; mul_ceil where rounding down would let an agent use more than it has) and how any total is split (alloc::allocate). Data stores are World tables and columns, or data files.
design.erd: Follow docs/DATA_MODEL_M5_M6.md: every entity is a struct-of-arrays table (D8), a relationship is a column holding another table's row index, and each table's kind (definition, topology, load-time derived, state) is stated. New money holders appear in World::total_money (D5).
design.classDiagram: Adapt it to D8: each table is a class whose attributes are its Vec columns, each tick system is a class with the stereotype <<system>> whose operation is the system function's signature, crates are namespaces, associations are row-index references. No inheritance between simulation entities (D8, AGENTS.md §1); say so in the text.
design.architecture: Say where any new system runs in the tick order (D4) and how parallel work reduces (AGENTS.md §3: integer sums only).
design.feasibility: Recurring cost includes the per-tick cost against the D13 budget.
design.tests: A conservation case per new money flow, determinism at 1/2/3/8 threads, and a bench run (D13) if a hot loop changes.

risks: hot loops under the D13 budget (docs/PERFORMANCE.md)
